description: A hackathon prototype of a live digital twin for emergency department patient flow. A built-in event simulator emits patient events such as arrival, triage, bed assignment and discharge onto Kafka; a Spring Boot service updates the twin state, held in Redis and stored in PostgreSQL, and an in-process Java discrete-event engine projects the next hours of flow to show bottlenecks before they form. Staff can run what-if scenarios that change staffing, bed counts or triage rules, and an LLM layer turns the results into a plain-language explanation with ranked recommendations. Wait-time predictions cover triage, bed and length of stay, and events and scenarios are stored for replay. Coverage: one generic emergency department, fed by simulated events. Access: free GitHub repository, run with Docker Compose. Caveats: the README calls it a prototype, real hospital feeds are only a design intention, and the licence appears only as a badge. Useful for capacity planning and testing emergency department operations in simulation; related records are not yet linked.
